chapters.title: Chapter 11: Landmark Standing Precedents—Lujan, Summers, Akins, and Florida Audubon
chapters.reason: This chapter teaches the core tests and doctrinal language that define Article III standing (injury in fact, causation, redressability) and the limits on procedural and informational injuries. Including excerpts from Lujan, Summers, Akins, and the en banc Florida Audubon decision is essential so students can read the Court's precise formulations (e.g., ‘‘concrete and particularized’’; Summers’ discussion of procedural rights without concrete harm; Akins’ informational-injury rule; Florida Audubon’s calibrated relaxation of imminence/redressability). The primary holdings and key textual passages are necessary source context for doctrinal analysis and classroom citation.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Landmark Administrative and Redressability Precedents—Heckler v. Chaney and Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine
chapters.reason: This chapter centers on judicial review limits tied to agency nonenforcement and standing when relief depends on third-party choices. Excerpts from Heckler v. Chaney and FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine are materially important to show the canonical Chaney presumption against review, the Court’s framing of enforcement discretion, and Alliance’s articulation that standing cannot rest on speculative independent third-party action. Direct quotation of those opinions is needed to ground discussions of causation, redressability, and exceptions to nonreviewability.
